feat(ui): G2b â€” the read views, refusal matrix and route-mapping gate (#303) (#368)

* feat(ui): carry the full Â§C.3 refusal table and render failures through it (issue #303 G2b)

G2b's first slice: ui_refusals.REFUSAL_ROWS carries ui-contract.md Â§C.3's
15 rows (the 14 interface error codes plus no-response) as RefusalData,
pinned character-for-character against the contract table by the new
suite (G2a pinned the single unauthenticated row; UNAUTHENTICATED_REFUSAL
is now a reference into the table, not a copy). The failure page renders
the code's own row beside the message and correlation id (GW-11: never a
softer code), and render_no_response carries GW-12's presentation half â€”
sent status UNKNOWN plus the reconcile link to run_find's view (the
mutating-form half is G3's, design D2). create_app exposes the seam as
app.state.ui_operations so the induced-code matrix can monkeypatch the
adapter's own operations object.

RED: ModuleNotFoundError 'benchweave.interfaces.ui_refusals' (collection
error, exit 2) before the module existed; the failure-page arm red on
the row-less G2a failure.j2. GREEN: 6/6 new tests; interfaces_ui 68/68.
ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy 0 (347 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§2.4, Â§7-F

* feat(ui): the G2b read pages â€” bench, run, request, evidence, document, artifact (issue #303 G2b)

Six read routes, each the rest.py three-step translation with the Identity
from the server-side session: /benches/{id} (bench_get + device_list +
the first events page, GW-20), /runs/{id} (run_get â€” status, outcome and
terminal state exactly as reported, no cancel control: GW-55's render
half), /requests/{id} (run_find â€” GW-12's reconcile view; control-tier in
the frozen catalog, so observe renders the honest forbidden row),
/evidence/{id}, /documents/{sha256} (digest shown, content bounded by the
adapter's one payload ceiling), /artifacts/{id} (chunked artifact_read
within max_chunk_bytes with the COMPLETE digest verified before the
response completes and reassembly bounded â€” GW-60/61). The three inline
G2a unauthenticated refusals collapse into one construction site.

RED: with register_read_pages neutralized on a scratch copy, 9/9
read-view tests fail ('assert 404 == 200' on /ui/benches/sim-bench â€” the
routes fall through to the UI's own 404). GREEN: 9/9; interfaces_ui
77/77. ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy 0 (349 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§2.4

* feat(ui): device pages render plugin presentation through the gateway's own validator (issue #303 G2b)

The device page resolves the plugin's presentation attachment from
admitted documents â€” envelope, manifest, binding catalogue and assets,
all content-addressed (a new read-only documents_by_schema_suffix query,
newest admission first) â€” and validates through
presentation.admission.validate_attachment, the same bytes the SDK host
uses (SW-41 parity). The gateway declares no custom panels and no named
UI features: a required panel the host lacks renders SW-41's
panel_unavailable refusal; an optional one renders unavailable. Readings
tiles populate only from gateway-reported observations (GW-22): G2 has
no observation lane, so tiles render Unavailable â€” never a submitted or
fabricated value; staleness (GW-23) is the contract predicate on the
observation's own age, wired at reading_staleness and pinned at the
composition seam. Dataset pages render the declaration skeleton with no
draw claims (design D3, #310's plot wrapper owns the draw); configuration
pages list declared presets read-only. create_app threads the content
store into the UI composition.

RED: ModuleNotFoundError 'benchweave.interfaces.ui_presentation'
(collection error, exit 2) before the module existed. GREEN: 5/5 new;
interfaces_ui 82/82; ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy 0 (351 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§2.4

* feat(ui): the GW-10 route-mapping gate with its planted-route kill control (issue #303 G2b)

ui_routes.UI_ROUTES declares every mounted /ui route â€” path, methods, the
seam operations the handler calls, and its classification (interface /
session / assets / shell) â€” and route_mapping_violations is the checker:
both directions (a mounted route without a row reds; a row without a
route reds), every mutating method must map to EXACTLY ONE of GW-10's
eight mutating operations (G2 mounts none â€” the session trio is flagged
non-interface, and the non-interface set is itself asserted complete,
R7's scope-creep tripwire). The suite enumerates the mounted sub-app's
own routes (this FastAPI wraps included routers lazily; the enumeration
unwraps effective_candidates().original_route). Two kill-control arms
prove the checker polices: a planted mutating /benches/{id}/runs POST
and a planted undeclared read route each produce a violation naming
them.

RED: ModuleNotFoundError 'benchweave.interfaces.ui_routes' (collection
error, exit 2) before the module existed. GREEN: 7/7 new (both planted
arms among them); interfaces_ui 89/89; ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy 0
(353 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§7-D

* test(ui): the G2b acceptance arms â€” observe-no-control, I02 /ui, the induced-code matrix (issue #303 G2b)

Â§7-E: an observe session renders every observe-tier view 200 with its
seam data (run_find is control-tier and change_get admin-tier in the
frozen catalog â€” the PRD's 'every read view' resolves against the
catalog, each pinned at its own tier); no page carries a form or button
(GW-55's cancel wording is G3's); a direct POST to every read path is
refused (the CSRF guard's 403 fires before the GET-only route table's
405 â€” either shape is a refusal, neither reaches a handler). Â§7-C's /ui
half: a posted principal is ignored (the strip shows the session's
principal), the adapter constructs Identity only in the session-record
mapping, and a cross-principal reconcile lookup renders not_found. Â§7-F's
data-bearing arms: artifact over the reassembly bound is
payload_too_large (control: under-bound downloads 200), a malformed
document digest is invalid_request (control: a well-formed unknown
digest stays not_found), the expired session renders unauthenticated
(induced through the session store's injected clock â€” the seam the whole
suite freezes), and the nine read-wire-impossible classes render their
rows via monkeypatched seam refusals, each with the uninduced control
asserting 200 first (cursor_expired is emitter-less in the seam â€” the
arm proves the page renders the row, not an emission).

RED: the suite's own discrimination is proven per-arm by the inline
controls (an arm that cannot discriminate cannot pass); the underlying
behaviours were RED at their landing commits (f28b7a5, 58f9e09, 84ac2c8).
GREEN: 18/18 new; interfaces_ui 107/107; ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy
0 (354 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§7-C/E/F

* feat(ui): the G2b browser lane, host CSS and the CON-5 amendment (issue #303 G2b)

The gateway-page browser lane (design Â§7-H's G2b half): one module-scoped
uvicorn server on an ephemeral loopback port serving the composed gateway
with seeded data; axe at WCAG 2.2 AA on every gateway page template, both
themes (prefers-color-scheme emulation â€” D7); the planted-violation
control from G1d's lane (a stripped button must red, proving the axe
configuration detects in the served context); and obligation 26's pins â€”
interactive targets at the 24px minimum on the rendered pages, the host
CSS's box-shadow rules are all none (SR-B2: the host adds no glow), and
the host declares no token of its own (the limiting border stays the
package's). The lane's structural quirk is documented in-file:
sync_playwright's driver leaves a loop in the main thread that
create_app's asyncio.run pin sweep cannot coexist with, so the server
fixture composes first (the browser fixture depends on it).

The device page's reading tiles now render through the package's Â§E.1
reading-tile partial (contract conformance for the tile rules) instead of
hand-rolled markup; host.css gains the read-page furniture (fact lists,
device lists, the events table, document content) with colour from the
token themes only. CON-5's amendment lands (the /ui session adapter is a
third transport over the one seam; its identity comes only from the
server-side session; its refusals render the contract envelope's own
code; I02/I09 cover it like REST and MCP â€” I09's half is G2c's). The
operator guide gains a read-only-UI section (STE register).

RED: the lane's arms red before the host CSS (the 24px arm measured
browser-default link heights) and the planted-violation control reds
against the stripped button â€” the measurement discriminates. GREEN:
browser lane 16/16 (12 axe page-theme arms + control + 3 obligation
pins); interfaces_ui non-browser 107/107; ruff 0; fresh-cache bare mypy
0 (355 files).

Refs: .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md Â§7-H, Â§8

* fix(content): pin admission ordering â€” a same-digest re-admission is idempotent (issue #303 G2b, lane-2 F1)

put_document used INSERT OR REPLACE on the documents sha256 PK: a
re-admission of IDENTICAL bytes deleted and re-inserted the row, minting
a fresh rowid that shadowed genuinely-newer admissions in every
rowid-ordered read â€” the presentation-attachment resolution picked a
STALE envelope (the lane's three-put repro: put v1, put v2, re-put v1 ->
compose picked v1). The content-addressing justification in the
resolution's docstring was false under REPLACE.

The fix is structural: ON CONFLICT(sha256) DO NOTHING. Both directions
of the ruling are pinned â€” a re-admission of the SAME digest is
idempotent (rowid and stored_at preserved, the first admission's row is
immutable for that digest); a NEW digest is a new admission (fresh
rowid, newest). Three store-suite arms (the three-put repro, the
idempotent re-put with the rowid/stored_at witness, the
new-digest-new-admission arm) plus the page-level three-put arm in the
UI consumer suite.

RED (quoted): 'the re-admitted identical v1 shadowed the newer v2
admission' (store + page arms); 'a same-digest re-admission minted a new
admission identity ((1, 2026-10-03T01:00:00Z) -> (2, 2026-10-03T09:00:00Z))'.
GREEN: 17/17 across both suites; focused+faults 211/211 (content/ is
state-adjacent â€” tests/faults/ run per the fold rules); ruff 0;
fresh-cache bare mypy 0 (355 files).

Refs: lane-2 F1 (MEDIUM); .claude/deep-review/2026-10-03-issue303-g2-readonly-ui-design.md

* test(ui_html): restore the canonical registration after the meta controls (issue #303 G2b battery)

A latent xdist order-fragility, exposed by the F1 fold's +4 tests: the
meta-acceptance controls in test_artifacts_meta deliberately empty or
shrink the module-global artifact registry and restore only some of it
(test_empty_registry_fail_closed_pure_function leaves it EMPTY; the
one-artifact control leaves exactly one). Under pytest -n auto the
doc-collected row items (docs/internal/ui-contract.md::row::*) share
each worker's process, and any row item the worker runs after the
residue fails 'no canonical artifact for <row>' â€” the pre-fold
distribution happened to be benign; the fold's test-count shift moved
108 row items onto the poisoned worker. A module-local autouse fixture
restores the full canonical registration after every control (clear
first: ensure_registered is sentinel-idempotent, so after the
one-artifact control a bare call would no-op). No conftest.py â€” a
second conftest module collides with tests/integration/conftest.py
under the config-driven bare mypy build.

RED: the full battery at the fold tip - 3416 tests, 108 failures, all
'no canonical artifact for <row>' on one xdist worker. GREEN: battery
3416/0/0, exit 0; ui_html + gate-wrapper + harness 548/548; ruff 0;
fresh-cache bare mypy 0 (355 files).

Refs: lane-2 F1 fold battery; the residue mechanism is the
registry-mutation hygiene class, proposed to the memory ledger

[chore] AI-assisted flaky E2E test fixes (#17517)

## Summary

Automated PR to fix flaky E2E tests identified from recent CI runs.

This PR was created by the `ai-fix-flaky-e2e-tests` workflow using
`grok-4.7-xhigh`.

## Changes

# Flaky E2E test fixes

Looked at the top 10 flaky Playwright tests from the last 4 days. Only
tests that failed in a local reproduction were changed. Tests already
marked `@pytest.mark.flaky` were left alone.

## Modified

### `e2e_playwright/st_data_editor_config_test.py`

`test_markdown_cell_keyboard_shortcuts` (chromium)

The markdown cell overlay (`.gdg-clip-region`) sometimes never mounts
after a double-click. This showed up locally on chromium while reopening
the cell after Ctrl/Cmd+Enter save: the saved markdown was already in
the widget return value, and the canvas accepted the double-click
without opening the overlay.

Added `_open_markdown_cell`, which double-clicks the cell and retries up
to 3 times until the overlay is visible. Both opens in this test use
that helper.

Verified with 10/10 passing chromium runs after the change.

These were not changed because 25 local runs passed, or because they are
already marked flaky:

-

`st_pydeck_chart_select_test.py::test_pydeck_chart_multiselect_has_consistent_visuals`
â€” already `@pytest.mark.flaky`

> 
> **Overview**
> Stabilizes the chromium-only
**`test_markdown_cell_keyboard_shortcuts`** Playwright test for
`st.data_editor` markdown columns.
> 
> Adds **`_open_markdown_cell`**, which double-clicks a row and retries
(up to 3 times) until the markdown cell overlay (`.gdg-clip-region`) is
visibleâ€”covering the case where the canvas accepts clicks before cells
are interactive after a rerun, so the overlay never mounts. It also
handles **`PlaywrightTimeoutError`** from `click_on_cell` when the
overlay is already up, avoiding extra clicks that would time out.
> 
> The keyboard-shortcuts test now uses this helper for the initial open
and for re-opening the cell after save, instead of a single
`click_on_cell` + `get_open_cell_overlay` sequence.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit
6af59b811e40cf0020b1580124d0543d268bba08. Bugbot is set up for automated
code reviews on this repo. Configure
[here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

records.commit_message:
Fix runtime filter toggle visibility bug + add Playwright UI regression suite (#85)

* fix: hide inactive runtime filter input group when toggling display mode

The .filter-group { display: flex } rule had the same CSS specificity
as the browser default [hidden] { display: none } rule, so the author
style silently won and the "hidden" minute-only or hours+minutes
filter group kept rendering. This made both sets of runtime filter
inputs visible at the same time regardless of the "Show Runtime in
Minutes"/"Show Runtime in Hrs & Mins" toggle state.

Add a more specific .filter-group[hidden] rule so toggling the runtime
display mode correctly shows only the matching filter input group
(min/max minutes, or min/max hours & minutes).

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* test: add Playwright UI regression suite for site/ (prevent filter toggle regression)

Add a browser-based UI test suite using pytest-playwright to catch
regressions that pure unit tests can't, such as CSS rules silently
overriding JavaScript-driven visibility toggles (the bug fixed by the
previous commit in this branch).

- tests/ui/conftest.py: serves site/ over a local HTTP server for the
  test session and mocks data-{region}.json network responses via
  Playwright route interception, so tests are deterministic and never
  read or mutate the real generated site data files.
- tests/ui/test_runtime_filter_toggle.py: covers the runtime display
  toggle showing only the matching filter input format (minutes-only
  vs. hours+minutes), value conversion between formats, min/max
  validation, reset-to-defaults, and basic movie rendering. Verified
  these tests fail against the pre-fix CSS and pass against the fix.
- pyproject.toml: add pytest-playwright as a dev dependency; add
  `poe test-ui` and `poe install-browsers` tasks; exclude tests/ui
  from the default `poe test` / coverage run since it exercises the
  static website rather than the platelet_movie package.
- .github/workflows/test-pr.yml, test-main.yml: install the Playwright
  Chromium browser and run `poe test-ui` in CI.
- README.md: document the new poe tasks and UI test suite.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix SonarCloud S9100: use return instead of yield in site_page fixture

The site_page fixture had no teardown logic after the yield statement,
so SonarCloud flagged it as a code smell (no teardown in this fixture).
Switched to return since there is nothing to clean up after the test.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address Copilot review feedback on PR #85

- Reword the CSS comment explaining the [hidden] override: clarify it's
  about author-vs-UA stylesheet origin at equal specificity, not rule
  ordering.
- Remove accidental duplicate 'poe lint' line in README examples.
- Make the toggle-visibility regression test wait for each post-click
  state via expect(...) before the next iteration reads it, removing a
  potential race on slower CI runners.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin CI Poetry version to 2.4.1 to match poetry.lock generator

poetry.lock was regenerated with Poetry 2.4.1 (added pytest-playwright),
but CI still installed Poetry 2.0.1. Align both workflows so 'poetry
install' doesn't risk incompatibility with the lockfile format.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin devcontainer Poetry install to 2.4.1

Match the Poetry version now pinned in CI (test-pr.yml/test-main.yml)
and used to generate poetry.lock, so the devcontainer, Codespaces, and
CI all install dependencies with the same Poetry version.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin remaining CI workflows to Poetry 2.4.1 for consistency

deploy-github-pages.yml, pr-movie-report-test.yml, and
weekly-movie-report.yml all still installed Poetry 2.0.1, the same
stale pin flagged in test-pr.yml/test-main.yml. Align every workflow
and the devcontainer on 2.4.1 (the version that generated poetry.lock)
so all environments install dependencies consistently.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Pin devcontainer Poetry installer script to a commit SHA + checksum

Previously the devcontainer piped the mutable
https://install.python-poetry.org endpoint straight into python3,
which always serves whatever the latest installer script is. Instead,
fetch install-poetry.py from a specific commit SHA of
python-poetry/install.python-poetry.org, verify its sha256 checksum,
then run it. This matches this repo's existing convention of pinning
GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs for supply-chain integrity.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix SonarCloud S6506: enforce HTTPS on Poetry installer curl fetch

Add --tlsv1.2 --proto "=https" to the curl call that downloads
install-poetry.py, matching the flags already used for the Doppler
CLI install earlier in this script. This prevents curl from silently
following a redirect to an insecure (non-HTTPS) URL.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Harden Poetry installer download in devcontainer post-create.sh

- Use 'trap ... EXIT' to remove the temp installer file on any exit
  path (success, checksum failure, or early error), not just after the
  final rm at the end of the script.
- Add curl's -f flag so an HTTP error response (e.g. 404) fails fast
  with a clear curl error instead of silently writing an error page to
  disk and only failing later at the checksum comparison step.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix README manual pytest example to exclude tests/ui

The 'Running Tests Manually' example ran 'pytest tests/ ...' directly,
which would also collect tests/ui and can fail unless Playwright's
Chromium browser is installed. Add --ignore=tests/ui (matching the
poe test task) and a note pointing to the UI test section.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Remove hard-coded PR number references, describe the fix instead

Both the test module docstring and the README's UI test coverage list
referenced 'PR #85' directly. Replace with a description of the actual
CSS specificity fix so the docs/tests stay accurate if backported or
referenced outside this PR.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Polish comments and formatting for continuity

- Align the new poe task entries (test-ui, install-browsers) with the
  rest of the [tool.poe.tasks] table's column formatting, which had
  drifted out of alignment.
- Clarify the devcontainer Poetry-install comment: distinguish the
  installer *script*'s pinned commit SHA from the Poetry *package*
  version pinned via --version, and note it should stay in sync with
  the version pinned in the CI workflows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
